blindSummary: Subnational anti-discrimination law here covers gender identity, and this state/province holds shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions. It is one of 16 states plus the capital district shielding patients, families and providers of gender-affirming care from civil or criminal exposure created by other jurisdictions' bans (covering 38% of the transgender population aged 13+); 2 more shield by executive order (6%), and 32 states and 5 territories have no such protection (56%). No adverse measure specific to this state/province is documented beyond the national framework; the only recorded differences from protective peers are resident-facing insurance details.
blindSourceSummaries: Anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map, July 2026 edition (an LGBTQ news site's republication of an activist publication's state-by-state map): rates this state/province in its protective grouping alongside 14 states and the capital district, based on regional non-discrimination law and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state prosecutions; records the July 2026 shifts - one state became the fourth-ever entry in the map's most severe travel grade after its felony bathroom ban carrying up to 5-year sentences, and another rose a band after extending its bathroom ban to universities - and details the federal layer behind the map's most severe national grading (passport sex-marker freeze, M/F-only airline data feeds, funding withdrawals).

LGBTQ policy-research project equality map of transgender healthcare 'shield'/refuge laws (data as of 25 September 2026): 16 states plus the capital district shield patients, families and providers of gender-affirming care from civil or criminal exposure created by other states' bans (covering 38% of the transgender population aged 13+); 2 more shield by executive order (6%); 32 states and 5 territories have no such protection (56%). This state/province is among the shield-law jurisdictions its protective rating rests on.
blindLocalsOnly: The only recorded differences from protective peers are health-insurance coverage details for gender-affirming care that apply to residents; a visitor never encounters them.
